meta.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

lesson.title: React useEffect Hook Tutorial
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Import useEffect and create counter state
steps.instructions: Import useEffect alongside useState in MyComponent.jsx, then create a count state and an addCount handler. Render the count and an Add button.
hints: Which hook do you need to import next to useState at the top of the file?
Use the updater function form setCount(c => c + 1) inside addCount.
Add useEffect to the named import from "react", initialize const [count, setCount] = useState(0), and wire <button onClick={addCount}>Add</button>.
common_mistakes: Calling addCount() directly in onClick={addCount()} instead of passing the function reference

steps.title: Update document title on every render
steps.instructions: Call useEffect near the top of MyComponent with a callback that sets document.title to the current count. Omit the dependency array so it runs after every re-render.

explanations.topic: Running useEffect after every re-render when dependencies are omitted

hints: Where should useEffect be placed inside the component?
Pass an arrow function to useEffect that assigns a template literal to document.title.
Write useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }); above addCount.
common_mistakes: Using single quotes instead of backticks for the template literal `Count: ${count}`
Placing useEffect inside a conditional or nested function instead of the top level of the component

steps.title: Run useEffect only on mount
steps.instructions: Pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so the effect runs only once when the component mounts. Test with a static title or click Add to verify the title no longer updates on re-renders.

explanations.topic: Using an empty dependency array [] for mount-only effects

hints: What second argument tells React that an effect has no dependencies?
Add a comma after the callback function inside useEffect and pass [].
Update the closing of your hook to }, []); so document.title is only set once on mount.
common_mistakes: Passing [] inside the callback instead of as the second argument to useEffect
Expecting document.title to keep updating when clicking Add while [] is present

steps.title: Add count dependency and Subtract button
steps.instructions: Add count to the useEffect dependency array so the title updates whenever count changes. Then add a subtractCount function and a Subtract button.

explanations.topic: Running useEffect on mount plus when a dependency value changes
Difference between [count] and omitting the dependency array

hints: Put the state variable name inside the dependency array.
Duplicate addCount, rename it to subtractCount, and change + 1 to - 1.
Change }, []); to }, [count]); and add <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to wrap count in square brackets as [count]
Wiring the Subtract button onClick to addCount instead of subtractCount

steps.title: Add color state and multiple dependencies
steps.instructions: Create a color state initialized to "green", add a Change Color button that toggles between "green" and "red", and style the count paragraph with that color. Include color in document.title and in the dependency array [count, color].

explanations.topic: Why missing color in dependencies leaves document.title stale
Re-running the effect when any dependency in the array updates

hints: Use a ternary operator inside setColor to flip between "green" and "red".
Remember JSX inline styles take an object inside curly braces: style={{color: color}}.
Update the dependency array to [count, color] and set document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`;.
common_mistakes: Using single curly braces style={color: color} instead of double curly braces style={{color: color}}
Forgetting to add color to [count, color] so the title stays stuck on green

steps.title: Initialize window width and height state
steps.instructions: Clear the previous counter code and create width and height state variables initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight. Display both values in paragraph elements.
hints: Which browser window properties return the viewport width and height?
Initialize two useState hooks with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.

Render

Window Width: {width}px

and

Window Height: {height}px

inside return.
common_mistakes: Misspelling innerWidth or innerHeight with incorrect camelCase
Forgetting to clear the old counter handlers before returning the new JSX

steps.title: Register resize listener inside useEffect
steps.instructions: Define handleResize to update width and height from the window object. Register the "resize" event listener and log "EVENT LISTENER ADDED" inside a mount-only useEffect hook.

explanations.topic: Why adding event listeners outside useEffect attaches duplicates on every re-render
Why React Strict Mode runs useEffect twice in development

hints: If window.addEventListener is placed directly in the component body, when does it run?
Move window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) inside useEffect(() => { ... }, []).
Write handleResize() to call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
common_mistakes: Leaving window.addEventListener outside useEffect, causing hundreds of duplicate listeners on resize
Omitting the [] dependency array on the event listener useEffect

steps.title: Return a cleanup function from useEffect
steps.instructions: Return an arrow function from the resize useEffect hook that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED".

explanations.topic: How returning a cleanup function from useEffect frees resources on unmount or re-render

hints: How do you tell useEffect to run cleanup code when the component unmounts?
Return a function at the end of the useEffect callback.
Add return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); } inside useEffect.
common_mistakes: Calling window.removeEventListener directly inside useEffect instead of returning a function
Passing a different function reference to removeEventListener than the one passed to addEventListener

steps.title: Add second useEffect for document title
steps.instructions: Add a second useEffect hook below the first one that updates document.title to `Size: ${width} x ${height}` whenever width or height changes.

explanations.topic: Using multiple useEffect hooks in a single component

hints: Can a React component call useEffect more than once?
Add a second useEffect call with [width, height] as its dependency array.
Write useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to include both width and height in the dependency array
Trying to put the document.title update inside the mount-only useEffect where width and height would stay stale
